unit.why: A short anecdote about the Besht in Istanbul opening one of R. Naftali Ha-Kohen's amulets. It is retold by R. David Moshe, who adds a homiletic explanation.

stories.start_quote: פ"א סיפר המעשה שבעת שהיה הבעש״ט
stories.end_quote: הוי כהוגה את השם וכו׳ ודפח"ח
stories.summary_en: On his journey to the Land of Israel the Besht, in Istanbul, had one of R. Naftali Ha-Kohen's famous amulets opened and found only R. Naftali's own name written in it; R. David Moshe draws from this an explanation of the rabbinic rule that one who calls his master by name is liable to death.
